CORE APPLICATION WORKFLOW

01 / THE PROBLEM

Agreement is only the start.

Freelance collaboration needs more than a job listing. Clients and freelancers need clear scope, agreed terms, staged delivery, feedback, and a record of changes.

I built FreelanceChain to connect those steps in one application, with separate workspaces and permission checks for each role.

02 / WHAT I BUILT

A complete collaboration flow.

  • Client workspace: project briefs, proposals, applicant comparison, versioned offers, and milestone reviews.
  • Freelancer workspace: project discovery, proposals, agreement acceptance, private task boards, and staged submissions.
  • Shared workrooms: conversations, authorized file access, notifications, and live workspace updates.
  • Administrator tools: support handling, reported cases, and eligible account and project moderation.
Feature walkthrough ↗Workflow details ↗
03 / ARCHITECTURE

One browser origin. Clear boundaries.

Browser → Vercel
React interface and same-origin /api requests

Vercel API proxy → Render
Express routes, authorization, application workflows, and server-sent events

Render → MongoDB Atlas
Application records, sessions, and private attachment storage

Render → Google Gemini
Optional milestone drafting and semantic applicant comparison

The frontend forwards API requests through its own origin to support cookie sessions and CSRF protection. Private uploads use MongoDB-backed storage in the deployed demo, avoiding reliance on temporary hosting filesystems.

Hosting design ↗
04 / ENGINEERING DECISIONS

The details behind the screens.

  • Session security: opaque HttpOnly cookies, hashed session tokens in MongoDB, expiry limits, and session revocation.
  • Server authorization: role and ownership checks protect project actions and private resources; CSRF validation protects authenticated changes.
  • Workflow consistency: versioned offers preserve agreement history, while milestone dependencies control delivery progression.
  • AI fallback: Gemini assists with planning and applicant comparison; guided planning and regular comparison remain available when AI requests fail.
  • Operations: liveness and readiness endpoints distinguish a running process from available database and storage dependencies.
Security implementation ↗AI integration ↗Hosting checks ↗
05 / VERIFICATION

Make the behavior reviewable.

The repository documents automated checks for authentication, core hiring and milestone workflows, storage access, recovery, and hosting configuration. The frontend uses Jest and React Testing Library; backend checks use the Node.js test runner.

Core hiring and milestone delivery flows have also been exercised on the deployed demo. These are documented project checks; they do not imply an independent security audit or complete production coverage.

06 / TRADEOFFS & NEXT STEPS

What I would improve next.

Free hosting can sleep between visits, and background reminders depend on the backend being awake. Live-event distribution is process-local; multiple backend instances would need shared event delivery.

Next steps include operational monitoring, a controlled production backup and recovery rehearsal, and independent labelled data for evaluating applicant matching. No verified real-world AI accuracy percentage is claimed.

This is a deployed project demonstration. Payments, escrow, and blockchain transactions are outside the implemented scope. Google sign-in remains in Testing mode.
